sources: FAA NASR 28-day subscription, cycle effective 2026-10-01; NAV_CSV, ILS_CSV, FIX_CSV zips (https://nfdc.faa.gov/webContent/28DaySub/extra/01_Oct_2026_<NAME>_CSV.zip)
FAA d-TPP cycle 2610 approach plate PDFs for roles/minima
_provenance.method: Extracted by scripts/extract-nasr-airport.ts PHL KPHL. ILS rows with ARPT_ID == PHL; navaids named in kphl-procedures.json navaids_referenced; fixes = every 5-letter fix named in fixes_and_roles of an instrument approach and every fix of a STAR transcription (stars[].star) in that file (each also checked against NASR FIX_BASE and, in charted_on, FIX_CHRT).

primary_navaid.name: WOODSTOWN
remarks: DME UNUSBL 090-105; 045-065 BYD 20 NM BLW 2500 FT.
primary_navaid.location_note: KPHL has no VOR/DME of its own: the only on-field NASR navaid is PHL VOT 109.8 (VOR test facility, 39.86528 N 75.23365 W), which is not a navigation aid. OOD (WOODSTOWN VORTAC 112.8, chan 75X, 39.63607752 N 75.30305627 W, NJ, OPERATIONAL RESTRICTED) is the VORTAC named as the missed approach hold of most KPHL ILS/RNAV plates and is used as the primary navaid.

ils_localizers.note: Six ILS/LOC systems with DME at KPHL (NASR ILS_BASE): runway 9L I-VII 108.95 (CAT I), 9R I-PHL 109.3 (CAT IIIB), 17 I-MYY 108.75 (CAT I, OPERATIONAL RESTRICTED), 26 I-LLH 111.55 (CAT I, localizer offset), 27L I-GLC 109.3 (CAT I), 27R I-PDP 108.95 (CAT I). Runway 35 and runway 8 have no ILS or LOC. The plates call 9L/27R I-VII/I-PDP and 9R/27L I-PHL/I-GLC; each pair shares a frequency (interlocked at opposite ends of one runway).
